page: Amazon Web Services c4.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 2.9 GHz, the CPU includes 25 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX, FMA, and AES instruction sets. The instance is equipped with 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 1.88 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the c4.4xlarge in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test scores 15219.95, while the single-core test reaches 1440.69. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate read-only speeds of 851.49 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 89.52 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In application-specific workloads, the server achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 7354.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 15674.33. However, database performance is mixed, with Passmark database operations scoring 5697.42 but Redis SET operations performing weakly at 6.16 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4.4xlarge provides a balanced hardware profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require high memory density or local storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing performance, making it suitable for tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving. It is also capable of handling light machine learning tasks, processing 135M parameter LLM prompts at 872.74 tokens per second, though performance drops significantly on larger models. This makes the instance best suited for batch processing, distributed analytics, and compute-bound web applications.
